sense: luck, what happens without a cause

terms.comment: By chance: cāsū or forte (see happen, by chance).

terms.grammar: noun, third declension: found only in the nominative and the ablative (forte)
evidence: Ter. Ph. 138: quod fors feret, ferēmus aequō animō

terms.comment: To trust to luck: fortūnae sē committere (Cic. Att. 9.6.4, Lewis & Short); personified, the goddess Fortune.

phrases.latin: cāsus ubīque valet; semper tibi pendeat hāmus: quō minimē crēdās gurgite, piscis erit
phrases.english: chance rules everywhere; keep your hook always dangling: in the pool where you least expect it, there will be a fish

phrases.latin: Quod fors feret, ferēmus aequō animō.
phrases.english: Whatever chance brings, we shall bear calmly.

phrases.latin: Fortūna vitrea est: tum cum splendet frangitur.
phrases.english: Luck is glass: just when it shines, it breaks.

sources: Lewis & Short: casus · Lewis & Short: fors · Lewis & Short: fortuna
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 155, 342.
